transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Singh (Redwood SE); Dr. Maya Rao (Horizon Bio Head of AI); Tom Alvarez (CTO); Sofia Perez (Security Lead); Evan Lee (Infra)

Auto-summary: Customer is highly regulated (HIPAA-like workflows), requires on-prem air-gapped deployment. Primary concerns: how we do offline updates, signing and transport of model/artifacts, integration with their HSM, and minimum hardware for acceptable latency.

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm alex with redwood, priya's our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Tom: Hi all, tom here. we'll let maya lead on the ML side; i'm here for infra questions.
[00:13] Maya: thanks, yeah, we want to explore a full onprem air-gapped deployment, we can't send PHI out, plus strict change control.
[00:22] Priya: great, can you walk us through existing infra, like what GPUs, how many nodes, network isolation, patch windows?
[00:30] Evan: currently we have a mix of A100 40GB and older A100 80s in two racks. no H100 yet. interconnect is standard PCIe, some nodes have nvlink. we're on k8s but air-gapped so updates are manual.
[00:46] Priya: ok, that helps. we support both hosted and private; for your case private onprem with airgap is the fit. we do an offline install artifact bundle and a signed image you can transfer via usb or internal mirror.
[00:58] Sofia: how do you handle key management? we can't have keys stored outside the ring.
[01:03] Alex: we integrate with customer KMS/HSMs, and for onprem we can do a customer-managed KMS with no keys leaving your environment. the agent that does the onboarding can be configured to use your HSM for signing.
[01:14] Maya: and audit logs? we need immutable logs for model requests and admin actions for audits.
[01:20] Priya: we emit detailed audit logs, and for private deployments those logs stay on your syslog/elastic or S3-equivalent. you control retention and we provide the schema.
[01:28] Tom: what's the update cadence? we operate change windows monthly, can't have constant pulls.
[01:34] Alex: we do offline patch bundles. our recommended flow is monthly signed bundles — you test in staging, then import to production during your window. Priya can share the offline update playbook.
[01:44] Evan: network wise, how much egress is needed? can devices be fully air-gapped except for initial transfer?
[01:50] Priya: yes, it's designed to be fully air-gapped. the runtime doesn't phone home. only initial artifact transfer and optional telemetry (which is configurable/disabled). we provide an import script and verification steps (sha256 + signature).
[02:05] Sofia: curious about model updates — do you allow bringing your own model (BYOM) and do you support quantized variants?
[02:12] Priya: absolutely BYOM. we support various quantizations and also recommend profiles based on your latency/cost tradeoffs. for onprem we ship a model bundle that includes variants. note sometimes the model names are transcribed funny in our docs, sorry.
[02:26] Maya: latency — for our app 200ms p95 is target per inference for a 1.2k token prompt. what's realistic on A100/PCIe?
[02:34] Priya: with A100 and nvlink you'll get better perf. without nvlink on PCIe, expect higher latency; quantization and batching help. rough ballpark: single token latency could be 30-50ms on A100, end-to-end p95 depends on prompt length and batching. we'll run benchmarks in the pilot.
[02:53] Tom: what about orchestration? we use k8s but offline. does Redwood need a control plane that sits outside?
[02:59] Alex: for private onprem we offer two modes: self-managed control plane inside your VPC/k8s cluster, or a lightweight customer-only control plane with no external services. nothing needs to be managed by the public redwood control plane unless you opt-in.
[03:14] Evan: can you do upgrades without internet? like sign bundles locally and then apply?
[03:19] Priya: yes, signed bundles are the mechanism — we provide tools to create and verify signatures. customers can bring their own signing keys stored in HSM.
[03:26] Sofia: encryption at rest and in transit?
[03:28] Priya: TLS for in-transit, and we support disk encryption with customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. logs and KV cache — sorry, sometimes i say KV cash — the kv cache can be encrypted and stored on your encrypted volumes.
[03:44] Maya: are there any constraints on model size or GPU memory? we have some LLMs ~70B that prefer 80GB cards.
[03:51] Priya: model size matters — 70B models generally need 80GB or sharding. we support sharded deployments but for best latency single-node 80GB (or H100) works. if you only have 40GB A100 you'll need more nodes or quantization.
[04:06] Tom: curious about fallback strategies — if a node is overloaded can requests route to a dedicated hosted fallback? we can't send PHI though.
[04:13] Alex: routing policies can be set at the request level. for PHI you can disable any external fallback. many customers use dedicated non-PHI fallback for non-sensitive workloads.
[04:23] Evan: what about hardware drivers and CUDA versions — we have a locked-down driver baseline; can your runtime work with older drivers?
[04:29] Priya: we have a matrix of supported CUDA and driver versions. part of the onboarding we'll validate and if needed package a compatible shim. sometimes we request driver updates but we try to avoid it.
[04:40] Maya: procurement question — what does a pilot look like? we want a 3-node cluster for benchmarking, run typical prompts, and a security review.
[04:48] Alex: pilot typically 4-8 weeks: install, baseline benchmark, tuning (batching/quantization), and security review. we'll propose a config and ballpark costs.
[04:57] Sofia: on legal, we need an SLA and explicit non-exfiltration clause. can you provide a legal addendum?
[05:03] Alex: yes, we have enterprise terms and can add an addendum; i'll route that to legal.
[05:09] Tom: any references with similar air-gapped installs?
[05:12] Priya: we've done installs with pharma and finance customers; i'll include anonymized case notes.
[05:18] Maya: cool. also curious about model lineage — we need to know which model version served each request for auditing.
[05:25] Priya: we record model version, commit id, and serving profile in the audit logs.
[05:31] Evan: do you have an offline inference runtime only? we'd like to keep control of orchestration entirely.
[05:36] Alex: yes, we can provide runtime artifacts and a helm chart you can install and manage. the console ops features can be optional and run inside your network if you want them.
[05:44] Maya: ok let's talk timeline — we're targeting a pilot in early Q2. procurement and security signoff are blockers.
[05:51] Alex: understood. we'll send the security package and propose dates. last thing — any immediate blockers we didn't cover?
[05:58] Sofia: just confirm again the signed bundle verification steps and that no keys leave our HSM.
[06:04] Priya: yes, we'll include a step-by-step with expected hashes and verification commands.
[06:09] Tom: thanks all.
[06:11] Alex: recap: Alex to send security docs and legal contacts; Priya to prepare pilot config and benchmark plan; schedule deep-dive with Evan. we'll follow up by email with proposed dates. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
